SEF 101 0
HACK independent BG shake -GHS

adjudicated.jp: と叫びつつ、襲いかかる金髪の貴公子。
adjudicated.en: So shouts the gold-haired noble young man that's swooping down on me.
comments: More Pattern conflation: Taichi's the Aristocrat of Love. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The blond young noble shouting as he attacks is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: しかしそれはおかしいじゃないか。

adjudicated.assessment: The objection that this is strange is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 当時、やつは金髪ではなかったのだから。

comments: Referring back to the theater incident, which is before the blond Sakuraba. Not exactly sure what a first-time reader should make of this: maybe dream logic? blond, pushes him down, no longer blond. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The explanation that he was not blond at that time is accurate.

adjudicated.jp: でもどうでもいいことだ。
adjudicated.en: But that's just whatever.
comments: Well, it's strong evidence that Taichi didn't have silver hair back when he was in the mansion, so whatever my full-width asterisk. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The dismissal that it does not matter is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 最強の矛と無敵の楯を装備している桜庭は、もとより理屈の通じない相手だ。
adjudicated.en: Sakuraba is equipped with a lance that can pierce any shield and a shield that can stop any lance, so from the very start he was never an opponent that could be reached through reason.
comments: This refers to the (supposed) origin of the Japanese word for contradiction, 矛楯 mujun, lit. "lance shield". If you've played Ace Attorney (I think it's #2), you've heard it. "Equip" is very RPG-ish, it's not random but evocative of his memory leak. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The contradictory spear-and-shield equipment and resistance to reason are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 『避妊するから』
adjudicated.en: Sakuraba: 『IT'S CONTRACEPTIVE!』
comments: SEF 101 0
HACK independent BG shake -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The speaker promises to use contraception or protection. The English instead applies the adjective 'contraceptive' to an unspecified thing and loses the promised action.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'I'll use protection.'

adjudicated.jp: と言い訳がましく迫りくる。
adjudicated.en: That's the justification-like thing he tells me as he approaches.
adjudicated.assessment: The excuse-like delivery while he closes in remains recoverable.

adjudicated.jp: 避妊すると言いつつ肉体関係を強要してくる、桜庭自体を否認したかった。
adjudicated.en: If Sakuraba was going to force carnal relationships while saying it's contraceptive, then I wanted to reject him from the very body.
comments: 自体 means "himself" as in "Sakuraba himself", but the sarcastic undertone of the overliteral, as often in Tanaka, can't be missed. Taichi rejecting this Broken Sakuraba - who's himself in a similar Pattern to what Taichi has - is itself interesting, but there's more. I suppose the anti-gay message is sorta unsubtle, but the real point is the rejection of contraceptives as the excuse for sexual relationships. That's pretty damn Catholic, considering. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator wants to deny or reject Sakuraba himself for forcing a sexual relationship under that pretext. The English misparses 'himself' as a phrase about rejecting him from a body.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that he wanted to deny Sakuraba's very existence or reject Sakuraba himself.

highlights.text: reject him from the very body

adjudicated.jp: どうしてこんなことに？
adjudicated.en: Why is this happening to me?
comments: He honestly wants you to marry his sister, though he could've foregone all that crap about the Chinese mafia really, but then certain metaphors might not have worked anymore. Anyway, the family's not about the incest but Mankind, put together by whims of the author (self-insertion mixed with god-figure, complete with having gone mad) and the Good Fortune that is still the God of Coincidences e.g. the Christian one. Hum, that'll need a new translation too, won't it. Crap. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The question why this is happening is exact.

adjudicated.jp: 日記にひどいことを書いたせいか？
adjudicated.en: Are the mean things I wrote in my diary?
comments: See CCA0012, exact same word that referred to what he did to Touko. Touko's name conspicuous in its absence. He was keeping a diary BEFORE his exchange diary with Yusa, meaning it's not his exchange with her that causes this. In short, Sakakibara is most the likely source. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source asks whether this is happening because of the cruel things he wrote. The English drops the causal predicate and leaves an incomplete question about the things themselves.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Is it because of the mean things I wrote in my diary?'

highlights.text: Are the mean things I wrote in my diary?

adjudicated.jp: 天罰か？
adjudicated.en: Wrath of God?
adjudicated.assessment: The speculation about divine punishment is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 応報か？
adjudicated.en: Just recompense?
adjudicated.assessment: The speculation about retribution is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: ハンムラビ法典か？
adjudicated.en: The Code of Hammurabi?
adjudicated.assessment: The reference to the Code of Hammurabi is exact.

adjudicated.jp: そりゃ微妙に違うか？
adjudicated.en: Aren't they only slightly different?
comments: Well, they are. I hope I don't need to make tedious explanations as to why the ancient Code of Hammurabi (and its refinement of Eye for an Eye) isn't metaphorically incompatible with a Christian Divine Retribution. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The source singles out the immediately preceding comparison as perhaps slightly off. The English instead compares the whole plural set to one another and reverses the tentative self-correction.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Maybe that one's a little different?'

adjudicated.jp: 俺はと言うと、どこかで夢だと知りつつも、パニック状態になっていた。
adjudicated.en: Whatever it may be, while I still know it's a dream that came from somewhere, I still slip into panic mode.
comments: Interesting to notice that he's having a flashback/dream about a dream, so it's legitimate to compare this to the previous dream seen in the route with Nanaka. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: He knows at some level that this is a dream but panics anyway. The English attaches 'somewhere' to the dream's origin, inventing a provenance instead of locating his awareness.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'though somewhere in my mind I knew it was a dream.'

highlights.text: a dream that came from somewhere

adjudicated.jp: 『からだはいやーっ』
adjudicated.en: Taichi: 『My body, you caaan't!』
comments: PCP CCA0012

The simple joke is that he's having done to him what he's done to her in his imagination; the more complex less-joke is that this nukige-ish writing at least matches his encounter with Sakuraba, meaning it hints at the Mansion; the most complex is how, as said, Sakuraba is implement The Pattern on him. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The shouted refusal concerning his body is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 『お慈悲！』
adjudicated.en: Taichi: 『Have mercy!』

adjudicated.assessment: The plea for mercy is exact.

adjudicated.jp: 『けだもの～っ！』

comments: PCP CCA0012

adjudicated.jp: などと叫びながら、桜庭の体を突き飛ばそうとする。
adjudicated.en: And all that sort of shouts I make while I try to thrust Sakuraba's body away.

adjudicated.assessment: Despite awkward syntax, the shouted resistance and attempt to push the other body away are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 純潔をかけたレスリング。

adjudicated.assessment: The wrestling match with chastity at stake is exact.

comments: Ambiguous as to from whom, if I got the sneer thing right it should be obvious why: Sakuraba's transitioning into Yutaka. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The awkward English remains recoverable as seriously considering killing him.

adjudicated.jp: ぼかぼかと殴る。
adjudicated.en: Strikes that go thunk, thunk.
comments: Curiously, there's a SFX that would go perfectly with this, but there's no SFX in any console versions, only the shakes that I've added. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The repeated thudding blows are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 一発がうまくクリーンヒット。
adjudicated.en: One of them is a skillful clean hit.
comments: See CCA0002 -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: One blow successfully lands as a clean hit. The English turns the adverb of successful contact into a claim that the hit itself is skillful.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'One of them lands cleanly.'

adjudicated.jp: 桜庭は横転する。
adjudicated.en: Sakuraba flips over.
adjudicated.assessment: The sideways tumble is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 仰臥して意識を失った桜庭の股間が、不意に暴発した。
adjudicated.en: Supine, his sense lost, Sakuraba's nethers unconsciously discharged.
adjudicated.assessment: Unconsciously is supported by the explicitly unconscious subject. It nevertheless loses the source's suddenness and creates avoidable ambiguity about agency and manner.
adjudicated.remedy: State that the discharge happened suddenly while he was unconscious.

adjudicated.jp: 射精したのかと思ったら、桜庭の荷電粒子砲（自称）の先端からは、手品さながらに花束が突きだしていた。
adjudicated.en: While I thought whether he'd ejaculate, from the pointed tip of Sakuraba's Charged Particle Cannon (self-named) out blows a bundle of flowers, as in a magician's trick.
comments: Yutaka's fallen down the stairs, he thought he was dead, but whoops, he just hurt his leg and lost his memories. And here's die Zubkonshous cenZoring it. -GHSigmund
adjudicated.assessment: The narrator first thinks he has ejaculated, only for flowers to emerge. The English makes this a simultaneous question about a future ejaculation and loses the reveal structure.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'Just when I thought he'd ejaculated...'

highlights.text: While I thought whether he'd ejaculate

adjudicated.jp: ああ。
adjudicated.en: Aw.
adjudicated.assessment: The brief exclamation is preserved in context.

adjudicated.jp: なんて悪趣味な展開なんだ。
adjudicated.en: What a development in bad taste.
adjudicated.assessment: The condemnation of the development as being in bad taste is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 目を覆う。

adjudicated.assessment: Covering his eyes is exact.

adjudicated.jp: そこで目が覚めた。
adjudicated.en: And that was when I was awake.
comments: Literally means to just wake up, of course; but the kanji for "eye" and the one usually used in the verb "memorise" are of course pointers to major portions of the story. Stuff like "I remembered my eyes" sounds too silly, besides being technically incorrect, and this kind of sentence is too minor for that kind of overadaptation anyway, so I'm going with something that just sounds a little off. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Despite awkward aspect, the moment of waking is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「……シュールすぎる」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "...way too surreal."
adjudicated.assessment: The judgment that it was far too surreal is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: だいたいあいつに、人を押し倒す度胸なんてあるはずないのだ。
adjudicated.en: Besides, I wouldn't expect that guy to have the pluck to push himself on somebody.
comments: See CCA0011A. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The disbelief that the other man has the nerve to push someone down is preserved.

adjudicated.en: He's a fainthearted obou-chan.
comments: His molestations towards the ojou-san would get punished by her male counterpart, even if it's in a double-nested dream. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The honorific noun characterizes him as a sheltered or pampered young master. Leaving it as an unexplained romanization with an English suffix untranslated withholds that characterization.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'a fainthearted, sheltered young master' or an equivalent characterization.

adjudicated.jp: どうせなら見里先輩に逆レイプされる夢ならよかったのに。

adjudicated.assessment: The wish that the dream had instead involved the named senior forcing herself on him is preserved.

comments: Miyasumi Misato is dead. Witness the birth of rape demon Misato!!! Seriously, Misato the Rape Demon just doesn't work. Except, thematically... -GHS

adjudicated.jp: 素敵すぎる……。

adjudicated.assessment: The judgment that the fantasy is too wonderful is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: うっとりしながら着替えた。

adjudicated.jp: メモもあった。

adjudicated.assessment: The presence of a note as well is exact.

adjudicated.jp: 『しっかり食べて行ってらっしゃい』
adjudicated.en: 『Eat properly and have a nice day』
comments: This is likely intended to fit with the passive-aggressive, weirdly written notes by Youko. Pretty interesting that the two would share this habit. Well, more like convenient to the point of it being inordinately suspicious. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The instruction to eat well and the send-off are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 美人でキャリアな睦美おばさんは、料理もうまい。
adjudicated.en: Beautiful career woman Mutsumi-obasan is also good at cooking.
adjudicated.assessment: Her beauty, career, and cooking skill are preserved.

adjudicated.en: She's so busy that she's almost never home, though.
comments: This is pretty normal in Japan; not for the host families of a know psychopath, however. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her being so busy that she is almost never home is exact.

adjudicated.jp: 頭が下がる。
adjudicated.en: I bow my head to that.
adjudicated.assessment: I bow my head to that can function as an English expression of admiration or respect and closely tracks 頭が下がる. No confirmed source error is established.
adjudicated.remedy: Optional idiomatic revision; no confirmed source-bound correction is established.

adjudicated.jp: お言葉に甘えて、分厚いサンドイッチを野菜ジュースで流し込んだ。
adjudicated.en: Presuming upon her kind offer, I wash down a thick sandwich with some vegetable juice.
comments: Wait a second 分厚い !!!MUTSUMI'S SANDWICHES ARE SAKAKIBARA'S DIARY AND HE JUST ATE THEM NOOOOOO!!! but seriously, Mutsumi's sandwiches seem few, while Youko's many. She also doesn't provide drinks, meaning CCA0004 should be Youko, again making sense of him visiting Tasaki. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Accepting the offer and washing down a thick sandwich with vegetable juice are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 時間がない。
adjudicated.en: I don't have time.
comments: But he wakes up so regularly, and Yusa's just about to leave...? -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The lack of time is exact.

adjudicated.jp: 残りはラップに包んでポケットに入れた。
adjudicated.en: I pack back the leftovers in the wrapping and put them into my pocket.
comments: No bag, few leftovers. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Despite awkward phrasing, wrapping the remainder and putting it in his pocket is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 途中で食べていこう。
adjudicated.en: I'll eat on the way.
adjudicated.assessment: The plan to eat it on the way is exact.

adjudicated.jp: さんさんと自己主張する日差し。
adjudicated.en: The rays of the sun assert themselves with brilliance.
adjudicated.assessment: The brilliant sunlight asserting itself is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 朝からこれだ。
adjudicated.en: This starts all the way from morning.
adjudicated.assessment: The awkward line remains recoverable as the oppressive condition already holding from first thing in the morning.

adjudicated.jp: 気が滅入る。
adjudicated.en: I feel depressed.
comments: Here I got nothing. Maybe he just hates the sunlight. I sure do *current time 2AM* -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: His depressed feeling is exact.

adjudicated.jp: しばらく歩いていると、
adjudicated.en: And after I've been walking for a while,
adjudicated.assessment: The transition after walking for a while is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「あぎゃらおーーーーーーーーっ！！」
adjudicated.en: Sakuraba: "Ah'gyarooooooooow!!!"
comments: 8xー -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The extended inarticulate scream is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 桜庭の悲鳴だ。
adjudicated.en: That's Sakuraba's scream.
adjudicated.assessment: Identifying it as the named person's scream is exact.

adjudicated.jp: わりと近い。
adjudicated.en: It's relatively near.
adjudicated.assessment: Its relative nearness is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 犬の吠え声と、悲鳴がさらに重なる。
adjudicated.en: The howl of a dog further overlaps the scream.
adjudicated.assessment: The dog's barking overlapping the continuing scream is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 遠ざかっていく。
adjudicated.en: And then they fade away.
adjudicated.assessment: The sounds growing more distant are acceptably conveyed as fading away.

adjudicated.jp: 「なるほど……」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "I get it..."
adjudicated.assessment: The realization is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 得心した。
adjudicated.en: I was satisfied.
comments: The puzzle solved, he loses interest. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Satisfied can mean convinced by an explanation. The wording is context-sensitive but does not necessarily replace comprehension with contentment.
adjudicated.remedy: Optional idiomatic revision; no confirmed source-bound correction is established.

adjudicated.jp: と、そこに―――
adjudicated.en: Then, right there---
adjudicated.assessment: The transition to something appearing right there is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「はれ？　太一さん？」
adjudicated.en: Girl: "Oh my? Taichi-san?"
comments: Oddly, not Senpai. He probable talked her into this. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The surprised recognition and address are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「おはよう」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "'Morning."
adjudicated.assessment: The casual morning greeting is exact.

adjudicated.jp: 「あ、おはようですっ」
adjudicated.en: Girl: "Ah, good morning, yes!"
adjudicated.assessment: The bright, slightly formal greeting is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: ぺこりと頭を下げる。
adjudicated.en: She bows her head with a sharp bob.
adjudicated.assessment: The quick bobbing bow is accurately conveyed.

adjudicated.jp: 近所に住む美少女の遊紗ちゃん。
adjudicated.en: This is Yusa-chan, the beautiful young girl that leaves near me.
comments: She lives on the other side of the road from him, technically. For the curious, she dropped the second 'u' because when she transferred from Upper Misaka she decided to eliminate all 'u'gly things (sorry, but the Higurashi joke is irresistible). -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The line identifies a beautiful girl who lives nearby. The English uses 'leaves' instead of 'lives,' reversing the residence verb through a mechanical word error.
adjudicated.remedy: Replace 'leaves' with 'lives.'

adjudicated.jp: 上見坂いい街。
adjudicated.en: Nice town Kamisaka.
adjudicated.assessment: Despite fragmentary English, the judgment that the town is nice is clear.

adjudicated.jp: 説明不要なほど可愛い遊紗ちゃんの、両手にカレーパンが揺れていた。
adjudicated.en: Yusa-chan, so cute it doesn't require exposition, held a loaf of curry bread swaying in her hands.
comments: Someone seems tired of exposition... anyway, Yusa is holding Christianity in her hands, and as for its swaying, see below. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her self-evident cuteness and the curry bread swaying in her hands are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 二人で並んで歩き出す。
adjudicated.en: The two of us line up and set out to walk.
adjudicated.assessment: The two beginning to walk side by side is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 別に今日にはじまったことでもない。
adjudicated.en: It's not really something that began today,
comments: Trollsplanation as to why this didn't happen the day before. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The observation that this did not begin today is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: なにせ同じ学校に向かうのだから。
adjudicated.en: it's because the two of us are going towards the same school anyway.
adjudicated.assessment: The reason that they are heading to the same school is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 後ろから、『い゛っでら゛っしゃーい！！』というハスキーな声が聞こえた。
adjudicated.en: From behind us I could hear a 『Habe a nice daaaaaaaay!』 in a husky voice.
adjudicated.assessment: The husky, distorted send-off heard from behind is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 遊紗ちゃんの母君だ。
adjudicated.en: That is Yusa-chan's mother.
comments: Somewhat polite, though not haha-ue-sama. First-time readers could be thinking that she is the one making him dinner. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The voice is correctly identified as her mother.

adjudicated.jp: ちょっと重くていらっしゃる。
adjudicated.en: She's sort on the heavy side,
comments: Suuuper important. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The intended euphemism that she is sort of on the heavy side is clear, but the missing 'of' creates a mechanical grammar error.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'sort of on the heavy side.'

adjudicated.jp: が、毎日楽しそうに生きておられるから、よしとしよう。
adjudicated.en: but it's all fine, since she lets me have something enjoyable every day.
comments: Same as above, the food, not just Yusa. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The mother herself appears to live happily every day, which the narrator takes as sufficient. The English instead claims she provides him with daily enjoyment, changing the subject and inventing a benefit to him.
adjudicated.remedy: Say that she seems to enjoy life every day, so he will call it fine.

highlights.text: she lets me have something enjoyable every day

adjudicated.jp: 平凡な家庭に生まれた美少女。
adjudicated.en: A beautiful girl that was born to a family this mediocre...
adjudicated.assessment: The beautiful girl born into an ordinary family is preserved, with a sharper English judgment of mediocrity.

adjudicated.jp: ただ一つ難点があるとすれば、世間を知らなすぎること。
adjudicated.en: If I had to find a just one blemish in her, it'd be that she is completely clueless of all things worldly.
adjudicated.assessment: The duplicated determiner and adverb make a mechanical grammar error in an otherwise accurate statement that her one flaw is excessive naivety.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'just one blemish' or 'a single blemish.'

adjudicated.jp: そんな遊紗ちゃんの、異性の先輩として一番身近な俺に課せられた責任は小さくない。
adjudicated.en: As the most familiar Senpai of opposite sex to little Yusa-chan, the responsibility given me is no little thing.
adjudicated.assessment: Despite awkward syntax, his claimed responsibility as the closest older male student is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 「いってきまーす！」
adjudicated.en: Yusa: "I am going ooout!"
adjudicated.assessment: The elongated leaving-home call is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: 手を振り返す、その顔に反抗期の陰もなく。
adjudicated.en: She returns a wave of the hand, on her face not a shadow of that rebellious age.
comments: As in adolescence. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: Her returned wave and lack of any sign of a rebellious phase are preserved.

adjudicated.jp: どころか、第一次性徴さえまだなのではないかと思われる節もある。
adjudicated.en: Far from it, as it appears we're also at a time where even her primary sexual characteristics might not be there yet.
comments: As in adolescence. -GHS
adjudicated.assessment: The speculation that even primary sexual development may not have begun is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: ま、とにかく揺れているのだ。
adjudicated.en: Well, for now they're swaying.
adjudicated.assessment: The deliberately ambiguous return to something swaying is preserved.

adjudicated.jp: そう、遊紗ちゃんが手に持つカレーパンの袋のように。
adjudicated.en: Yes, just like that bag of curry bread that Yusa-chan has in her hands.

adjudicated.jp: 「可愛い後輩を、困らせたままにしておくようなハンカチじゃないんだよ」
adjudicated.en: Taichi: "Leaving a cute Kouhai in trouble is not worth a handkerchief."
adjudicated.assessment: He says this is not a handkerchief that would leave a cute junior in distress, valuing her welfare above the cloth. The English reverses the relation and says leaving her in trouble is not worth a handkerchief.
adjudicated.remedy: Use 'This isn't a handkerchief worth leaving a cute junior in trouble over.'

adjudicated.assessment: The narrator intensely wants to make the girl bear his children. The English attaches the intensity to how wholeheartedly she would bear a baby, changing whose desire is being described.
adjudicated.remedy: Attach the intensity to his desire rather than to her imagined action.
